PREFIX brick: <https://brickschema.org/schema/1.5/brick#>
PREFIX ref: <http://example.com/ref#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?point ?ts WHERE {
  ?point a brick:Pump .
  ?point rdfs:label "HWPump01" .
  ?power a brick:HasElectricPower ; brick:hasSubComponent ?point .
  ?power ref:hasExternalReference ?tsid .
  ?point ref:hasTimeseriesId ?ts .
}

PREFIX brick: <https://brickschema.org/schema/1.5/brick#>
PREFIX ref: <http://example.com/ref#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?s ?p ?o WHERE {
  ?s rdfs:label "HWPump01" .
  ?s ?p ?o .
}

PREFIX brick: <https://brickschema.org/schema/1.5/brick#>
PREFIX ref: <http://example.com/ref#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?id WHERE {
  ?id brick:hasName ?name .
  FILTER (CONTAINS(?name, "HWPump") || CONTAINS(?name, "HW_Pump") || CONTAINS(?id, "HWPump"))
}

PREFIX brick: <https://brickschema.org/schema/1.5/brick#>
PREFIX ref: <http://example.com/ref#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999-02-22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
SELECT ?id ?class WHERE {
  ?id a ?class .
} LIMIT 200

Found it. The tsid is `54bac0b6-bd85-5aca-861a-0399d378e5cc`, unit W. Now compute the mean on 2018-10-27.

input.code:
import csv
tsid = "54bac0b6-bd85-5aca-861a-0399d378e5cc"
day = "2018-10-27"
vals = []
with open(VALUES_CSV) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        if row["timeseries_id"] == tsid and row["timestamp"].startswith(day):
            vals.append((row["timestamp"], float(row["value"])))
vals.sort()
print("count:", len(vals))
for v in vals:
    print(v)
mean = sum(v for _, v in vals)/len(vals)
print("mean:", mean)
